text: ICAR Protocol for Rice Sheath Blight (Rhizoctonia solani): In humid Kharif conditions with RH > 85%, drain standing water for 48 hours to aerate canopy base. Apply bio-agent Trichoderma viride or Pseudomonas fluorescens at 2.5 kg/ha mixed with 50 kg well-rotted farmyard manure or foliar spray at 0.5% concentration. Avoid excessive synthetic nitrogen fertilizer which softens leaf sheaths.

ICAR Protocol for Rice Blast (Pyricularia oryzae): Symptoms include spindle-shaped lesions with grey center and brownish-red borders. Spray bio-fungicide formulation of Pseudomonas fluorescens (0.2%) or extract of botanicals (neem oil 3% + soap solution). Apply silica (potassium silicate) to harden leaf epidermis. Balance NPK by withholding nitrogen top-dressing during active blast lesions.

ICAR/IRRI Cooperative Protocol for Brown Plant Hopper (Nilaparvata lugens): Practice Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) irrigation; draining water exposes hopper nymphs to predatory spiders and mirid bugs. Spray 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE) directed at plant base. Never use synthetic pyrethroids which cause resurgence. BPH migrates on monsoon winds across Bihar-Bengal borders; alert neighboring districts when catches exceed 5 hoppers per hill.

ICAR Protocol for Bacterial Leaf Blight (Xanthomonas oryzae): Characterized by wavy yellow water-soaked streaks starting from leaf tips. Bleaching powder application at 5 kg/ha in standing water reduces bacterial inoculum. Spray bio-formulation of Plant Growth Promoting Rhizobacteria (PGPR) at 5 ml/L. Ensure field bunds are weed-free to eliminate wild host grasses.

ICAR Protocol for Wheat Yellow/Stripe Rust (Puccinia striiformis): Small yellow pustules aligned in linear stripes on leaf blades. Treat early localized foci with Trichoderma harzianum foliar spray. Ensure balanced micronutrient application (Zinc Sulphate 25 kg/ha) to boost crop immunity. In cool humid conditions, inspect low-lying waterlogged patches twice weekly.

ICAR Protocol for Wheat Loose Smut (Ustilago nuda): Entire ear converted into black powdery mass of spores. Solar heat treatment of seeds in May-June or biological seed inoculation with Trichoderma viride (10g/kg seed) provides systemic internal protection. Destroy infected ears by bagging before spore dispersal.

Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR) IPM Protocol: Install 5 pheromone traps per acre for pest monitoring. When trap catches exceed 8 moths/day for 3 consecutive days, release egg parasitoid Trichogramma bactrae at 60,000 eggs/acre at 7-day intervals. Spray 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE) to disrupt larval oviposition. Avoid late season picking to break pest lifecycle.

CICR Protocol for Sucking Pests (Aphids, Jassids, Whiteflies): Install 10 yellow and blue sticky traps per acre at crop canopy height. Spray entomopathogenic fungus Verticillium lecanii or Beauveria bassiana (5g/L) during humid evening hours. Conserve natural predators including green lacewings (Chrysoperla carnea) and ladybird beetles.

ICAR-IIMR Protocol for Maize Fall Armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda): Practice push-pull intercropping with Desmodium (repellent) and border Napier grass (trap crop). In early whorl stage (V3-V6), apply dry sand mixed with neem seed powder (9:1 ratio) inside central whorls. Spray entomopathogenic fungus Metarhizium anisopliae (5g/L) targeting central leaf cones.

ICAR Protocol for Maize Stem Borer (Chilo partellus): Intercrop maize with cowpea (2:1 row ratio) to encourage predatory fauna. Apply Trichogramma chilonis egg cards (50,000 parasitoids/ha) at 15 and 22 days after sowing. Remove and compost plants showing deadheart symptoms to prevent secondary generation emergence.

ICAR-IIPR Protocol for Chickpea Wilt (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. ciceris): Deep summer ploughing exposes fungal chlamydospores to solar heat. Seed biopriming with Trichoderma asperellum (10g/kg) and Rhizobium leguminosarum inoculant (20g/kg seed). Practice crop rotation with non-host cereals (Wheat or Barley) for minimum 2 seasons.

ICAR Protocol for Pulse Pod Borer (Helicoverpa armigera): Install T-shaped wooden bird perches at 15 per acre to invite insectivorous birds (drongos, mynas). Spray Helicoverpa Nuclear Polyhedrosis Virus (HaNPV) at 250 LE/ha in evening hours with 0.1% jaggery as feeding stimulant. Intercrop with marigold as trap crop.

ICAR-DRMR Protocol for Mustard Aphids (Lipaphis erysimi): Early sowing before October 20 escapes peak aphid infestation. Spray botanical neem oil formulation (3000 ppm at 5ml/L) or 2% soap oil solution when aphid colony reaches 2cm twig length. Ladybird beetle predators (Coccinella septempunctata) provide natural biological suppression.

ICAR-IISR Protocol for Soybean Yellow Mosaic Virus (YMV): Transmitted by whitefly (Bemisia tabaci). Grow 3-4 border rows of maize or sorghum as windbreak barriers. Spray 5% NSKE at 20 and 35 days after sowing. Rogue out and destroy early infected virus plants showing bright yellow mosaic patches within 30 days of sowing.

Soil Health Protocol for Acidic Soils (pH 5.0 - 6.2): Acidic soils induce phosphorus fixation and aluminum/manganese toxicity. Apply agricultural limestone or dolomite at 200-300 kg/ha broadcast during land preparation. Apply 5 tons/ha of well-aerated vermicompost to buffer soil cation exchange capacity. Inoculate seeds with Phosphate Solubilizing Bacteria (PSB) to unlock fixed soil phosphorus.

Soil Health Protocol for Sodic/Alkaline Soils (pH > 8.0): High sodium limits soil porosity and water infiltration. Apply agricultural gypsum (calcium sulphate) based on soil gypsum requirement test. Follow with green manuring of Dhaincha (Sesbania aculeata) incorporated at 45 days; organic acids released during decomposition neutralize alkalinity.

National Mission on Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA) Soil Carbon Protocol: For soils with Organic Carbon < 0.5%, practice in-situ crop residue management. Never burn stubble; spray waste decomposer formulation (200L/acre) over chopped residue and incorporate with rotavator. Incorporate green manure legumes into fallow windows to raise soil organic carbon by 0.15% over 3 seasons.

Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) Water-Saving Protocol: Install a perforated PVC field water pipe (15cm diameter, 30cm length) to monitor root-zone water depth. Re-irrigate only when water level drops 15cm below soil surface. AWD reduces greenhouse gas emissions (methane) by 30-40%, saves 25% pumping energy, and strengthens root anchorage against fungal foot rot.

Regenerative Agro-Ecosystem Practice: Follow Kharif Aman rice with short-duration relay legumes (Lentil, Green Gram, or Khesari) sown in standing rice 10 days before harvest (Paira cropping). Legume root nodules fix 35-45 kg atmospheric nitrogen per hectare, leaving residual fertility that reduces chemical fertilizer need for subsequent summer crops by 30%.

Agro-Meteorological Risk Rule: Sustained relative humidity above 80% combined with temperatures between 26-32°C creates ideal microclimate conditions for fungal blast, sheath blight, and mildews. Farmers should refrain from evening overhead irrigation, maintain clean field drainage ditches, and perform prophylactic bio-fungicide sprays prior to rain events.

Digital Public Good Accessibility Rule: For smallholders with keypad phones or intermittent connectivity, prioritize vernacular voice synthesis in regional dialects (Bengali/Hindi). Actionable advisories must emphasize exactly ONE immediate physical intervention (e.g. 'drain water' or 'spray neem extract') rather than complex chemical blends.

West Bengal Matir Katha Regional Guidance: In Nadia, Malda, and Murshidabad Gangetic alluvium soils, high water tables and summer monsoon humidity require focus on lodging-resistant varieties (Swarna-Sub1). Ensure zinc supplementation (Zinc EDTA 1.5g/L) during tillering to prevent Khaira disease.

Bihar DBT Krishi Regional Guidance: In Purnia, Katihar, and Saharsa agro-climatic zones, sandy loam to clay loam soils benefit from community seed banks. Monitor for stem borer in early Kharif and pod borer in winter chickpea. Use bio-fertilizer Azotobacter for non-legumes and Rhizobium for pulses.

Digital Agriculture Cooperation Mandate: Border districts of West Bengal (Malda, Uttar Dinajpur) and Bihar (Katihar, Purnia) share contiguous agro-ecological corridors. Community pest detections should automatically broadcast anonymized vector telemetry across state boundaries to alert extension officers 48 hours before swarm dispersion.
